answer: Latency triangulation: each agent identity must answer timed pings from five random verifiers on different continents every epoch. Step 1: verifiers send fresh nonces at an unannounced moment. Step 2: round-trip times place the responder in a region, a fingerprint as distinct as a pigment. Step 3: identities whose position and jitter overlap are merged into one. A clone farm in one canyon of racks cannot fake distance, as light speed is fixed, so each fake needs its own server in another city, about $30 a month; a zephyr of new seats cannot share it, so the attack stops paying.
